answer: Before acting, an agent must lock a bond forfeit if its identity proves fake. Clones are cheap to spin up but costly to fund, since each locks its own deposit. Every agent also weaves a thread of signed attestations linking it to prior work. When the protocol detects clones sharing a funder or copying that thread, it slashes their bonds and seizes the deposits. A lone sparrow and a meadow of copies face one rule: honest identities keep their stake, clones lose theirs.
